title: A parked tick's claim is invisible to the width, so the run over-claims
body:
A tick parked by a hold-only-its-tick refusal keeps its claim standing (window.go: a question this run parked keeps its tick's claim standing) and leaves the window, but the width's arithmetic (claimsHeld, window.go:1580) reads only the graph's dispatch.in_flight_ids and the plan's Claimed flags — both readings taken at the last replan, i.e. BEFORE the claim was taken. The next admission therefore counts fewer claims than the tracker holds and claims past the declared width; production tk 0.32 grants the claim instead of refusing it, so the over-claim is silent. Verified at the base: in the ceilingGate/linger-until shape of hold_test.go's TestATicksTerminalRefusalHoldsOnlyThatTick, a1 is tick_held with its claim standing, a2 is claimed and worked to the end, and the tracker counts 3 claims open at once under a declared width of 1 — and width 1 is the DEFAULT, the width every run whose gate declares no [orchestration] table runs at. Found by the lifecycle model's width invariant (tick 89g), which records the counterexample in InvariantTheDeclaredWidthIsNeverExceeded; the existing parkedClaims/endHeld code (window.go:1609, window.go:631) reads as though the authors intended parked claims to count, and the fix is a semantic decision — count them in the window's width, or release the claim on a park — not a mechanical one.
evidence: internal/reconcile/window.go:1470 (mayAdmit), window.go:1580 (claimsHeld), window.go:1609 (parkedClaims); internal/reconcile/lifecycle_pbt_test.go InvariantTheDeclaredWidthIsNeverExceeded has the minimal counterexample; reproduced at the base by asserting peak claims in the fixture of hold_test.go's TestATicksTerminalRefusalHoldsOnlyThatTick (3 at width 1)
